topic: Mean velocity and acceleration from a velocity–time graph
problem: Determine the mean velocity and the mean acceleration of a point in 5 and 10 seconds if it moves as shown in Fig. 6.
solution: The path travelled in the first 5 s is numerically equal to the area under the velocity–time graph and is 10.5 cm. Hence the mean velocity is 2.1 cm/s and the mean acceleration is 0.8 cm/s². The path travelled in 10 s is 25 cm; hence the mean velocity is 2.5 cm/s and the mean acceleration is 0.2 cm/s².
diagram_caption:
Fig. 6 is a velocity–time graph.

Horizontal axis: time t, measured in seconds.
Vertical axis: velocity v, measured in cm/s.

The graph is a continuous piecewise-linear polyline through the points
(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 3), (5, 4), (6, 4), (7, 3), (9, 2), (10, 2),
where each consecutive pair is joined by a straight-line segment.

The graph explicitly marks t₁ = 5 s and t₂ = 10 s.
source_note: Question, solution substance and trusted reconstruction caption supplied by the user. The original Fig. 6 image was not supplied for this P10 implementation, so the caption has not been independently checked against it. At the user’s instruction the reconstructed graph uses the caption alone. No independently located book, image, solution-derived area or inferred physical datum is used for graph reconstruction. The SVG is a reconstruction, not the original scan.
formal_interpretation: Define the caption polyline as a real velocity function in cm/s over seconds. Prove closed-segment interpolation, vertex values and nonnegativity on [0,10]. Derive segment integrals by FTC, add them at caption breakpoints and obtain displacements 21/2 cm and 25 cm. Prove path equals displacement here via nonnegative velocity. Derive the two time averages and endpoint-based accelerations. Keep graph data separate from the solution targets; no force, particle or mass model is used.
